hyperedges.label: Seema Labs Three Moments of Clarity
Three Corner Strokes of the Trinetra Mark

nodes.label: npm run check
nodes.rationale: Verifies local assets, section links, unique HTML IDs, and JavaScript syntax before publishing.

nodes.label: Google Fonts
nodes.rationale: Fonts load from Google Fonts with system fallbacks so the static sites need no package dependencies or build step.

nodes.label: Local Preview
nodes.rationale: Requires Node.js 18 or newer. npm start serves Seema Labs on port 4174; npm run preview:trinetra serves Trinetra on port 4173. PORT overrides the port. No npm install is needed.

nodes.label: Nepal
nodes.rationale: The company's connection to Nepal, and the Nepali meaning of Seema as boundary or limit, must be preserved in the sites.

nodes.label: Seema Labs
nodes.rationale: The company whose work is defining clear boundaries for autonomous AI systems. The name Seema means boundary or limit, and the connection to Nepal is meant to be preserved.

nodes.label: Static Hosting
nodes.rationale: Each website folder can be uploaded to a static host with index.html at the serving root. Pushing to GitHub does not update the existing hosted sites. Hosting credentials are omitted, and GitHub Pages is not enabled.

nodes.label: Trinetra
nodes.rationale: Seema Labs' first product. Company-site links to Trinetra are required to point at the existing hosted Trinetra website.

nodes.label: Nepal
nodes.rationale: The name story pairs Nepali roots (सीमा / Seema) with the problem of bounding useful AI autonomy.

nodes.label: Seema Labs
nodes.rationale: Named Seema, Nepali for boundary or limit, because the company defines clear boundaries for autonomous AI. Agents should have enough freedom for meaningful work while staying inside those limits.

nodes.label: Trinetra
nodes.rationale: First product: the boundary brought to the coding task. It turns a coding task into focused permissions, explains why each permission is needed, and leaves approval with people.

nodes.label: Trinetra
nodes.rationale: Turns a coding task into focused permissions, explains why each permission is needed, and gives people control over approval so teams can make deliberate decisions about what an agent can access and change.

nodes.label: Seema Labs Website
nodes.rationale: Static site in sites/seema-labs/, previewed at http://127.0.0.1:4174 via npm start. Existing host is https://seema-labs.zestycream11.chatgpt.site. No package install or build step; fonts come from Google Fonts with system fallbacks.

nodes.label: Trinetra Website
nodes.rationale: Static site in sites/trinetra/, previewed at http://127.0.0.1:4173 via npm run preview:trinetra. Existing host is https://trinetra-focused-access.zestycream11.chatgpt.site.

nodes.label: Hosted Trinetra Site
nodes.rationale: Outbound product links use https://trinetra-focused-access.zestycream11.chatgpt.site rather than an in-repo route.

nodes.label: Accessibility and Responsive Layout
nodes.rationale: Keyboard navigation, visible focus states, reduced-motion support, and responsive layouts must stay intact, and interactive controls should be reviewed in a browser before publishing.

nodes.label: Give AI Autonomy, Not Unlimited Authority
nodes.norm_label: give ai autonomy, not unlimited authority
nodes.rationale: Repository thesis: grant AI room to act while refusing unlimited authority.

nodes.label: Content Integrity Guideline
nodes.rationale: Do not invent customers, testimonials, pricing, contact details, certifications, or product guarantees.

nodes.label: Give AI Autonomy, Not Unlimited Authority
nodes.norm_label: give ai autonomy, not unlimited authority
nodes.rationale: Useful AI needs room to work and clear limits. Organizations define the boundaries of authority for autonomous systems. Closing line: build for autonomy and be deliberate about authority.

nodes.label: Access with Intention
nodes.rationale: Product stance: give coding agents the access their task calls for, with a clear purpose for every permission, and keep people in control.

nodes.label: Additional Access
nodes.rationale: Third moment of clarity: more authority deserves a new look. An agent request for extra access returns the reason to a person. A request is a prompt for a decision, not an automatic expansion of scope.

nodes.label: Human Review
nodes.rationale: Second moment of clarity: people review proposed permissions with their reasons and approve or deny the plan. The sample review is a browser-only decision, not a live grant.

nodes.label: Login Timeout Permission Example
nodes.rationale: Sample task 'Fix the login timeout bug' proposes read+edit on src/auth/session.ts and tests/auth/session.test.ts plus execute of npm run test:auth. Production secrets stay outside the plan; a separate read of .env.production requires another human review. Illustrative sample data, not a claim that every interface detail ships.

nodes.label: Policy Controls
nodes.rationale: Policy controls protect sensitive files. The sample marks .env.production as protected production configuration and warns that a non-sensitive timeout value may be enough.

nodes.label: Additional Access
nodes.rationale: New access starts a new conversation. When an agent asks for more authority, a person reviews what changed and why. A request for more access is a decision to review.

nodes.label: Human Review
nodes.rationale: Requested access and its explanation stay together so a person can approve or deny with context. The on-page review is an illustration.

nodes.label: Login Timeout Permission Example
nodes.rationale: Sample task 'Fix the login timeout bug' proposes read+edit on src/auth/session.ts and tests/auth/session.test.ts, execute of npm run test:auth, and shows .env.production as protected. A separate read-only request to compare the production session timeout is reviewed by a person. Interfaces use sample data.

nodes.label: Make the Call
nodes.rationale: How-it-works step 03: approve or deny the proposed access, and review a separate request if the agent needs more authority.

nodes.label: Illustrative Browser-Only Examples
nodes.rationale: Permission plans and approval controls are illustrative browser-only examples. They do not grant real access or contact a backend.

nodes.label: Human Direction
nodes.rationale: Principle 03: people and organizations should have a say in what authority is granted.

nodes.label: Human Review and Approval
nodes.rationale: Principle 03: give people the context and the choice to approve or deny.

nodes.label: Review When Scope Changes
nodes.rationale: Principle 05: bring additional access requests back to a person for a decision.

nodes.label: Boundaries for Sensitive Files
nodes.rationale: Principle 04: use policy controls to protect files that need extra care, such as production configuration.

nodes.label: Purple #7960dc
nodes.rationale: The only color in the file. Hex #7960dc (RGB 121, 96, 220) is the group stroke and the diamond fill. No other fills, strokes, or gradients appear.

nodes.label: Thick Round Stroke
nodes.rationale: The corner group sets fill to none, stroke-width to 5, and stroke-linejoin to round. Width 5 is one-eighth of the 40-unit canvas, so the corners are heavy strokes with rounded joins. The diamond path does not use this stroke.

nodes.label: Three Eyes Reading
nodes.rationale: Uncertain reading, flagged for review. The file path names the mark trinetra, and the drawing has three corner strokes, but the SVG contains no text and the strokes are open right-angle corners rather than drawn eyes.

nodes.label: 40 by 40 ViewBox
nodes.rationale: Root svg viewBox is '0 0 40 40'. The root has no width or height attributes, so the mark is a square coordinate system that scales with its container.

nodes.label: Bottom Corner Stroke
nodes.rationale: Path d='M8 24l6 11 12-6': polyline (8,24) to (14,35) to (26,29). The outer vertex is (14,35), at the bottom. The interior angle is about 92 degrees.

nodes.label: Central Purple Diamond
nodes.rationale: Filled path d='m20 15 5 5-5 5-5-5z' with fill #7960dc and no stroke. Vertices are (20,15), (25,20), (20,25), and (15,20): a square rotated 45 degrees, centered at (20,20), with horizontal and vertical diagonals of length 10.

nodes.label: Three Open Corner Strokes
nodes.rationale: A group element with fill none, stroke #7960dc, stroke-width 5, and stroke-linejoin round. It contains exactly three open path strokes and no closed shapes.

nodes.label: Trinetra Logo Mark
nodes.rationale: Single-line SVG mark on a 40 by 40 viewBox. No text, title, description, or circle elements. A filled purple diamond is centered, and a group of three thick open corner strokes in the same purple surrounds it.

nodes.label: Right Corner Stroke
nodes.rationale: Path d='M23 7l11 7-6 11': polyline (23,7) to (34,14) to (28,25). The outer vertex is (34,14), on the right. The interior angle is about 94 degrees.

nodes.label: Top-Left Right-Angle Corner
nodes.rationale: Path d='M18 5H6v12': polyline (18,5) to (6,5) to (6,17). The vertex is (6,5). One arm runs east and the other south, an exact 90-degree corner at the top-left of the canvas.

nodes.label: Permission Plan
nodes.rationale: First moment of clarity: a coding task becomes a focused plan that shows which files and actions are relevant and why each permission is requested.

nodes.label: Permission Plan
nodes.rationale: Permission planning attaches a reason to each proposed file or action. The task is the starting point; the explanation makes the plan reviewable.

nodes.label: Start with the Task
nodes.rationale: How-it-works step 01: describe what the coding agent should do. The task gives the permission plan its purpose.

nodes.label: Task Context to Human Judgment
nodes.rationale: Stated path from why Trinetra exists: task context, then clear permissions, then human judgment. A focused task should not imply whole-codebase access.

nodes.label: Understand the Access
nodes.rationale: How-it-works step 02: inspect the proposed files and actions with a clear explanation of why each is needed.

nodes.label: Understandable Decisions
nodes.rationale: Principle 04: permission requests should be clear enough to review.

nodes.label: Clear Explanations
nodes.rationale: Principle 02: make the purpose of each permission easy to understand.

nodes.label: Bracket Monogram Motif
nodes.rationale: The three strokes read as an opening square bracket, a broken closing bracket, and a hyphen through the gap, like a code or prompt glyph. The file does not name that reading.

nodes.label: Center Crossbar
nodes.rationale: Second path M15 20h23. Horizontal stroke from (15,20) to (38,20). It starts inside the left bracket, whose arms end at x=25, and runs through the right stem's gap, ending four units past x=34.

nodes.label: Possible Block Letter E
nodes.rationale: Uncertain alternate reading as a block E: left spine, short top and bottom arms, a longer middle bar, and detached right ticks. The ticks do not join the arms (gap from x=25 to x=34), and the file has no letter or title.

nodes.label: Split Right Stem
nodes.rationale: Same path continues M34 5v11 and M34 25v10. Two vertical ticks at x=34, from y=5 to y=16 and from y=25 to y=35, with a gap between y=16 and y=25.

nodes.label: Left Squared Bracket
nodes.rationale: First subpath M25 5H6v30h19. A square-cornered C opening right: top arm from (25,5) to (6,5), spine down to (6,35), bottom arm back to (25,35).

nodes.label: Burnt Orange Stroke #d55b35
nodes.rationale: Parent group sets fill none, stroke #d55b35 (burnt orange), stroke-width 4, and stroke-linecap square, so every segment is a thick blunt stroke with no fill.

nodes.label: Seema Labs Logo Mark
nodes.rationale: 40 by 40 SVG mark with no text and no circles. Two unfilled paths share one group: stroke #d55b35, stroke-width 4, square line caps. The drawing is a left squared bracket, a split right stem, and a horizontal bar through the middle.

nodes.label: AI Coding Agents
nodes.rationale: Agents can modify software, run commands, access tools, and touch development infrastructure, so organizations must decide which authority to delegate.

nodes.label: Defined Task Boundary
nodes.rationale: Hero diagram: AI activity stays inside a defined task boundary, with freedom to act within scope. Asking for more authority is a human decision. Marked as an illustrative concept so delegation stays deliberate.

nodes.label: AI Coding Agents
nodes.rationale: The product exists so teams can decide, with context, what a coding agent may access and change for a focused task.

nodes.label: Clear Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Principle 02: authority given to an agent should be defined for its task.

nodes.label: Useful Autonomy
nodes.rationale: Principle 01: AI agents should be able to complete meaningful work.

nodes.label: Task-Focused Access
nodes.rationale: Principle 01: connect the requested authority to the work at hand. A focused task deserves a focused scope; a login fix may need a few files, not an entire codebase.

nodes.label: Three-Eye Motif
nodes.rationale: Uncertain reading. Three separate strokes around a center can be seen as three eyes, and the filename is trinetra, but the SVG does not state that word or that meaning.

nodes.label: 40 by 40 ViewBox
nodes.rationale: viewBox="0 0 40 40" on the root svg. The diamond center (20,20) is the center of that box.

nodes.label: Violet #7960dc
nodes.rationale: The only color in the file. It is the stroke of the open contours and the fill of the diamond.

nodes.label: Center Filled Diamond
nodes.rationale: Filled path m20 15 5 5-5 5-5-5z. Vertices (20,15), (25,20), (20,25), and (15,20): a diamond, a square rotated 45 degrees, centered at (20,20).

nodes.label: Trinetra SVG Mark
nodes.rationale: Root svg with viewBox 0 0 40 40 and no width or height. No text elements and no circle elements. Two painted parts: a stroked group and one filled path, both in #7960dc.

nodes.label: Three Open Stroke Contours
nodes.rationale: One path inside a group with fill none, stroke #7960dc, stroke-width 5, and stroke-linejoin round. Three subpaths: top-left L from (18,5) to (6,5) to (6,17); right bend from (23,7) to (34,14) to (28,25); bottom bend from (8,24) to (14,35) to (26,29). None of the contours is closed.
